answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry resists fake identities: each agent locks a ferrous-hard deposit behind its public key, and every verified task adds weight to its record. New identities start on a thin ledge with no history, so they cannot outbid established agents for valuable work. Like water carving a karst cave, honest behavior slowly deepens trust, while a Sybil farm must pay the full bond for every clone, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
